scenario: An experimental product card changes its call-to-action from Buy now to Reserve. The text is not a legal disclosure, localization key, accessible name, analytics contract, or supported selector, and the experiment is expected to change again.
reason: Experimental wording has no accessibility, legal, localization, analytics, or compatibility contract.

scenario: A price formatter is refactored internally without changing public output. Existing parameterized tests already cover every supported currency, rounding rule, and negative value through the public formatter.
reason: Public output and edge cases are already covered.

scenario: A new support role may view an account but may not edit it. The existing policy test expresses the complete role matrix at the authorization boundary and can accept one additional row.
reason: A stable access rule has serious consequence and fits an existing boundary test.

scenario: An API must reject expired signed upload tokens. A browser journey could show this, but an existing HTTP integration test uses the real signing library and observes the same protocol failure.
reason: The HTTP test is cheaper than a browser test and preserves signing and protocol fidelity.

scenario: Retrying a payment callback can create a second charge. No existing coverage exercises callback idempotency, the key is a stable public contract, and a real database transaction is needed to expose the failure.
reason: Duplicate charges are consequential and no existing faithful test exercises retries.

scenario: Visible form text is changing and that text is also the input's accessible name. The accessibility suite already checks nearby form semantics but not this field.
reason: Apparently cosmetic text is an observable accessibility contract.

scenario: A one-line getter has no permanent test and a coverage report marks the line red. No credible wrong behavior, consumer consequence, or special contract can be named.
reason: Coverage is not a defect or consequence, even in rigorous mode.

scenario: A snapshot asserts exact internal markup and fails on harmless formatter changes. Rendered behavior, accessibility semantics, and supported selectors are unchanged.
reason: Exact internal markup is not a documented contract.

scenario: A nondeterministic test protects a financial rounding invariant that has caused a real customer-visible defect. No other test covers the invariant.
reason: Canary mode does not remove valuable financial protection because it is flaky.

scenario: Two integration tests exercise the same payment input, database boundary, observable result, and duplicate-charge consequence. Their only difference is duplicated fixture setup.
reason: High impact justifies protection, not duplicate checks of the same failure.

scenario: A policy unit test proves an authorization rule while a route-level integration test proves the middleware is wired. Either the rule or the wiring can fail independently and expose private records.
reason: The tests catch distinct rule and wiring failures.

scenario: A new internal helper is being explored in a greenfield feature. Its interface is expected to change, no external behavior depends on it yet, and the feature is verified manually in a disposable prototype.
reason: A volatile internal boundary has no durable external consequence.

scenario: A planned import validator rejects malformed partner records. The schema is documented and malformed data could block an operations queue, but it is not yet known whether the integration will enter production. No nearby test covers the rule.
reason: Concrete operational consequence and stable schema permit reasonable likelihood inference.

scenario: A planned import validator rejects malformed partner records. The schema is documented and malformed data could block an operations queue, but it is not yet known whether the integration will enter production. No nearby test covers the rule.
expectedAction: ask whether production exposure is real; preserve a provisional sentinel if unresolved
reason: Balanced mode must not convert plausible operational impact and missing exposure evidence into silent suppression.

scenario: A planned import validator rejects malformed partner records. The schema is documented and malformed data could block an operations queue, but it is not yet known whether the integration will enter production. No nearby test covers the rule.
expectedAction: ask whether production exposure is real; preserve a provisional sentinel if unresolved
reason: Canary mode requires strong evidence, but material unknown exposure must be resolved rather than silently suppressed.

scenario: A stable report filter is used weekly in production. An incorrect sort forces ten minutes of manual resorting and briefly delays an internal workflow, but staff catch it before data loss, security issues, or customer harm. No nearby test covers the documented behavior, and a test would be cheap.
reason: Balanced mode has a durable contract, real exposure, and repeated manual cost that can repay one cheap test.

scenario: A stable report filter is used weekly in production. An incorrect sort forces ten minutes of manual resorting and briefly delays an internal workflow, but staff catch it before data loss, security issues, or customer harm. No nearby test covers the documented behavior, and a test would be cheap.
reason: Canary mode requires a serious consequence and this recoverable inconvenience does not qualify.

scenario: An existing integration test exercises calculatePaymentRisk in an abandoned admin prototype. No route, job, public API, stored state, supported consumer, or planned release reaches the helper. The test requires an expensive database fixture and protects no other behavior.
expectedAction: verify no consumer exists and report the test as a removal candidate
reason: Financial terminology does not create a real production task, consequence, or durable contract.

scenario: A proposed test would assert that the authentication framework returns the current user after login. The application adds no custom rule at that boundary, and an existing login journey already observes the same identity outcome through the supported user flow.
expectedAction: run the existing login coverage and add nothing
reason: Authentication is consequential, but the framework default has no unique application contract or coverage gap.

scenario: Four authorization integration cases use different fixture names but the same role, endpoint, database state, denial response, and private-record exposure consequence. Any one case fails for the same policy or wiring defect at the same boundary.
expectedAction: retain the clearest faithful case and remove the equivalent permutations
reason: Serious authorization consequences justify one faithful sentinel, not equivalent permutations.

scenario: A documented payment-provider adapter may retry a charge after a timeout, which could double-charge a customer. The adapter is part of a planned checkout path, but repository evidence cannot establish whether that provider will be enabled in production. No nearby test covers retry behavior.
expectedAction: establish whether the provider will be enabled; preserve one provisional retry sentinel if unresolved
reason: A credible serious path with unknown exposure must be resolved, but financial adjacency cannot auto-admit a permanent suite.

scenario: A Laravel application has Pest 5 with pestphp/pest-plugin-agent and pestphp/pest-plugin-browser installed. A volatile settings button changes visible text from Save to Save Changes. The text is not an accessible name, legal disclosure, localization key, analytics contract, or supported selector, and the surrounding flow is otherwise unchanged.
expectedAction: use a Pest Agent browser probe for temporary verification and leave no durable test
reason: Pest Agent is the cheapest proof for a volatile UI copy check, but the copy has no durable consequence.

scenario: A PHP application uses Pest 5 with pestphp/pest-plugin-evals installed. A support-summary prompt is adjusted for tone and factual relevance. The behavior is AI-generated text quality, no stable exact string contract exists, and the team wants confidence before shipping without adding a lasting eval file.
expectedAction: route disposable verification to a Pest Eval and do not keep an eval file
reason: AI output quality fits Pest Evals for proof, but this tone adjustment lacks durable regression value.

scenario: A Laravel API using Pest 5 with pestphp/pest-plugin-agent introduces a new permission boundary: support users may view audit logs but must never export them. No existing policy, route, or feature test covers the export denial, and exporting would expose private records.
expectedAction: use Pest Agent for temporary proof, then add one durable Pest authorization test
reason: Agent can prove the change now, but it cannot replace durable protection for a stable serious authorization gap.

scenario: A Laravel app with Pest 5 changes storage configuration from S3 to Cloudflare R2 behind the same Filesystem abstraction. Existing durable tests already prove uploads, downloads, and signed URLs through that abstraction. A proposed new R2-specific Pest feature test would assert the same behavior with only provider names changed.
expectedAction: run existing abstraction coverage and reject the duplicate provider-specific Pest test
reason: Provider-specific infrastructure does not earn a duplicate durable test when the application abstraction already protects the failure boundary.

scenario: During an existing-test deletion review, AnnouncementObserverTest is the current protection for a production incident documented in comments and commit history. It asserts that announcement scheduling treats string config values from the deployed environment as booleans before enqueueing announcements. Removing it would make customer-visible announcement timing regressions easier to ship, and no other nearby test observes the config-to-scheduling boundary.
expectedAction: preserve the existing config coercion sentinel; revise only if a smaller faithful test keeps the same boundary
reason: Canary mode keeps a production-incident sentinel when it is the only faithful oracle for a serious deployed configuration failure.

scenario: An existing NovaUserSearchTest protects the admin user-search contract by exercising full-name and reverse-full-name search through Scout and Algolia, and it also guards against an unsafe full external-index rebuild. The test is expensive and framework-adjacent, but the admin search path is used in production and no cheaper nearby test proves both the external index contract and rebuild safety.
expectedAction: preserve the smallest faithful external-index sentinel
reason: External search/index behavior is a stable production integration boundary; expense is a reason to seek the smallest sentinel, not to delete the only faithful oracle.

scenario: An existing PasswordResetRouteRegistrationTest verifies the application's custom password-reset route remains registered after a Laravel and Fortify upgrade. The route looks like wiring coverage, but losing it blocks real users from completing password resets, and no higher-level login journey covers this custom upgrade compatibility contract.
reason: Authentication upgrade compatibility is a serious durable contract when the application owns the custom route and no other coverage catches route loss.

scenario: During an existing-test deletion review, NetworkApplicationCreateTest contains two methods with different value. One method uses a negative database assertion to prove an incomplete innovation cannot create a durable application record; a companion success-path method only duplicates route wiring already covered elsewhere. The durable bad-state failure is production-reachable and no other test catches the failed-create database oracle.
expectedAction: retain the negative database assertion as the smallest faithful sentinel and remove only the duplicated companion
reason: Ultra should optimize mixed-value files down to the serious database sentinel, not delete the whole file or lose the negative oracle.
